187 likes, 5 comments - bigleemurali on October 9, 2026: "A six-pack doesn’t automatically mean you’re fit. Neither does a 10K run or a 200 kg deadlift. 👇

Real fitness has TWO parts:
✅ Achieve your goal — fat loss, muscle gain, strength or performance.
✅ Protect your health — blood sugar, lipids, liver, kidney function and other relevant health markers.

You can look fit, lift heavy and still neglect your health.

Don’t just train for a better body. Build a healthier body.

Save this Reel as a reminder that fitness is more than what you see in the mirror. 📌

Follow @bigleemurali for practical, science-based fitness, nutrition and strength training advice.

#Fitness #BodyTransformation #StrengthTraining #HealthyLifestyle #FitnessIndia".

449 likes, 3 comments - bigleemurali on October 8, 2026: "5 supplements that may support healthy testosterone levels — when used correctly 👇
1. Vitamin D3 — 1,000–2,000 IU/day
Especially relevant if your vitamin D levels are low. Some studies have shown improvements in testosterone, but clinical trials are inconsistent—so test rather than blindly megadose. PubMed
2. Magnesium — 200–350 mg/day of elemental magnesium
Magnesium is involved in many processes related to hormone metabolism. Supplementation may be most useful when dietary intake is inadequate or deficiency is present. PubMed
3. Zinc — 10–15 mg/day
Zinc is important for normal testosterone production, particularly when zinc status is low. More isn’t necessarily better—avoid routinely exceeding 40 mg/day of elemental zinc unless medically indicated. PubMed
4. Tongkat Ali — 100–200 mg/day of a standardized extract
Human studies using standardized Eurycoma longifolia extracts have reported improvements in testosterone in some men, particularly those with lower testosterone levels. Product standardization matters. PubMed
5. Boron — 3–6 mg/day
Interesting, but the evidence is still limited. Small human studies have investigated doses around 6–10 mg, but there isn’t enough evidence to call boron a proven testosterone booster. PubMed
⚠️ The important part:
Supplements won’t compensate for poor sleep, excessive body fat, chronic stress, inadequate protein, alcohol excess or poor training.
Think of them as supporting the system—not fixing a broken system.
Before trying to “boost testosterone,” get your morning testosterone tested and address the fundamentals first.

Train smart. Build naturally. Optimize for the long term.
#Testosterone #MensHealth #NaturalBodybuilding #HormoneHealth #StrengthTraining".

At 25, you can get away with poor sleep, inactivity, stress, low protein and unhealthy habits.
At 40+, those choices start showing up in your strength, muscle mass, mobility, recovery, hormones and metabolic health.
Your body keeps the receipts.
Don’t wait for the bill. Start investing in your health now.
#HealthyAfter40 #StrengthTraining #HealthyAging #MuscleAfter40 #Longevity".

128 likes, 2 comments - bigleemurali on October 6, 2026: "90 kg can look completely different on two different people.

One can have 30% body fat.
Another can have 10% body fat with significantly more muscle.

Same weight. Completely different bodies.

This is why I don’t want you to obsess over the number on the weighing scale.

As a coach, I look beyond weight:

👉 Body composition
👉 Waist circumference
👉 Muscle & strength
👉 Fitness and performance
👉 Blood markers
👉 Lifestyle

Your goal shouldn’t simply be “I want to weigh X kg.”

The better question is:

“What kind of body and health do I want at that weight?”

Stop chasing a number. Start measuring progress that actually matters.

Save this reel if you’ve been struggling with the weighing scale—and send it to someone who needs to hear this.

#FatLoss #BodyTransformation #FitnessTips #StrengthTraining #HealthAndFitness".

138 likes, 4 comments - bigleemurali on October 5, 2026: "5 mistakes that are silently killing your fat loss 👇
If you’re working out, eating “healthy” and still not seeing the fat loss results you want, don’t immediately assume you need more cardio or fewer calories.
You may simply be missing these 5 fat-loss fundamentals:
1️⃣ Not eating enough protein
Protein helps support muscle retention while you lose body fat and keeps your meals more satisfying.
2️⃣ Skipping strength training
Fat loss isn’t just about seeing the number on the weighing scale go down. You want to preserve muscle and build a stronger body.
3️⃣ Ignoring sleep
Poor sleep can affect hunger, recovery, energy and your ability to stay consistent with your diet and training.
4️⃣ Drinking your calories
Sugary drinks, fancy coffees, juices and frequent liquid calories can quietly add up without making you feel as satisfied as a proper meal.
5️⃣ Moving only during your workout
One hour in the gym doesn’t cancel out an entire day of sitting. Walking and daily movement matter too.
The biggest fat-loss mistake?
Thinkin".
